tasks.short: Take payment at the counter by card, phone or cash, and give the right change.

steps.what: Counter worker tells the customer the total shown on the till
Customer pays by card or phone on the terminal, or hands over cash
Counter worker re-keys the amount on a card terminal not linked to the till
Counter worker counts cash tendered, keys it and counts out change
Counter worker hands over the receipt and order number
Counter worker sorts out a declined card or a customer short of cash

tasks.design: Link the card terminal to the {OTHER} point-of-sale till so the amount goes across and the payment result comes back without re-keying. Cash handling, receipts and payment problems stay with the counter worker; a cash recycler is an option only where volumes justify the cost.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate terminals from the bank were cheap and the till supplier charged for the link.
tasks.enabler_now: Most restaurant tills support integrated card terminals as a setting with the payment provider.
tasks.still_hard: Cash stays physical; counting change and calming a customer whose card fails is people work.
tasks.human_edge: Handling cash honestly and quickly and dealing kindly with a payment that fails.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; card payments take a few seconds less.

reach.task: Take payment at the coffee counter
reach.learn: Whether the same terminal link works on the bar's second till.

evidence.claim: Restaurant tills can pass the amount to an integrated card terminal and receive the payment result.
The tax authority advises a reliable register and a seven-year retention duty for hospitality businesses.
Whether a business may refuse cash follows national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the total shown to the customer leaving with a receipt; till closing is outside.
Input contract: order total and payment result per sale, produced by the till and the terminal; fallback is keying the amount by hand.
Outlets that already have integrated terminals save nothing here.
Customer time is outside the counter worker's savings.
unknowns: Whether the outlet's card terminals are already linked to the till.
research_questions: How often do card amounts get mis-keyed on unlinked terminals?

incremental.description: Counter worker restarts the terminal link and falls back to manual keying when it drops.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the payment provider links only some terminals, so half of card payments are still keyed and s3 keeps 50 (5.3); high: every terminal is linked (11.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the customer's order, key it into the till with options, compute the bill and pass it to the kitchen.

steps.what: Customer states the order at the counter
Counter worker asks size, sides, drink and eat-in or takeaway
Counter worker keys the order and modifiers into the till
Counter worker reads the order back and corrects mistakes
Counter worker applies meal deals, discounts and vouchers to compute the bill
Counter worker checks the final order on the screen before sending: items, options and eat-in or takeaway
Counter worker sends the order to the kitchen: calls out or writes the order slip today; one press sends it to the kitchen screen after the change

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} point-of-sale till with combo buttons, required modifiers and meal-deal rules that apply themselves, a customer-facing display that shows the order as it is keyed, and voucher scanning. The counter worker checks the final order and sends it with one press to the kitchen screen, so the slip and call-out go.
tasks.previous_blocker: Smaller outlets ran a basic till without a kitchen screen, and meal deals were applied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Restaurant tills route orders to kitchen screens and apply deal rules as settings; QR ordering connects to the same till.
tasks.still_hard: Customers change their minds and ask for off-menu changes; keying stays a person's job at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: Getting the order right with a hurried or unsure customer and suggesting a sensible extra.

ambition.what: QR ordering from the queue or table for customers who prefer it, feeding the same till and kitchen screen.

tasks.altitude: The counter worker keys and serves; no slips or deal arithmetic. Decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Read and complete orders from the kitchen screen
reach.learn: Whether required modifiers cut remakes in the kitchen.

evidence.claim: QR ordering lets guests order and pay, and the orders go to bar or kitchen through the till.
The vendor reports about 8% more transactions for restaurants using its QR ordering, and one UK bakery 20% higher spend per QR order.
Dutch menu prices include VAT and drinks carry different VAT rates, so each till item needs the right VAT code.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer stating the order to the order in the kitchen with a total; payment is outside.
Input contract: menu items with price, VAT code, required modifiers and deal rules, produced by the operations manager in the till's back office; fallback is manual price override.
Scenario: outlet has no kitchen screen today; where it has one, the slip saving is already taken.
Customer time is outside the counter worker's savings; QR ordering is counted only as ambition.

Asking for options and the check before sending keep their full time. s3 keeps 85 because combo buttons save keying separate items. s4 keeps 50 because the customer reads most orders on the display. s5 keeps 30 for keying odd discounts. s6 keeps 10 for the press and the odd call to the kitchen.
unknowns: Whether the outlet has a kitchen screen.
How meal deals are applied today.
research_questions: How many order errors per shift come from read-back misses?

incremental.description: Counter worker reports wrong deal rules or missing modifiers.
Operations manager keeps menu items, deals and modifiers current in the till.

approvals.approved_version: The order with items, options and eat-in or takeaway exactly as checked by the counter worker in s6c, sent once to the kitchen screen for that order number; any change needs a new check and a new send.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the outlet does not buy a kitchen screen and many deals still need manual overrides, so s6 keeps 100 and s5 keeps 60 (15.1); high: kitchen screen and deal rules work as designed (29.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: At end of shift, count the till drawer, balance it against the till's receipts and hand over to the manager.

steps.what: Counter worker prints the till's end-of-shift reading of receipts
Counter worker counts notes, coins and vouchers in the drawer
Counter worker matches card terminal total with the till's card receipts

Counter worker fills the balance slip and works out over or short: on paper today; after the change the worker enters the counts by denomination on the shift-close screen and the till works out over or short
Shift manager recounts if over or short, signs and drops cash in safe
Shift manager checks the shift closing before approving it: counted and expected totals per tender, the over or short and its note
Shift manager copies shift totals into the daily sales spreadsheet for finance

tasks.design: Use the shift-close screen of the {OTHER} point-of-sale till for a blind count by denomination; the till holds expected cash and card totals, takes the terminal's totals through the integration and shows over or short. The shift manager approves the closing in the till, and a nightly job sends approved shift totals to the {ERP} and a {BI} sales view, replacing the slip and the spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tills and terminals were separate, and small outlets relied on paper slips and a spreadsheet to reach finance.
tasks.enabler_now: Restaurant tills offer shift-close screens with blind counts, and their sales exports can feed the ledger.
tasks.still_hard: Counting cash stays physical; an over or short with no till trace still needs the manager's judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Counting carefully, explaining a difference honestly and keeping the drawer under control during the shift.

ambition.what: Area manager checks over-and-short by outlet every morning instead of at month end.

tasks.altitude: The counter worker counts and enters; no arithmetic or slips. The shift manager approves in the till.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of food preparation and serving workers
reach.task: Prepare the daily cash deposit and sales report
reach.learn: Which closing fields finance needs so the spreadsheet can go.

evidence.claim: Restaurant tills can run a blind shift count and show expected totals per payment type.
The tax authority advises a reliable register and a seven-year retention duty.
Per-person logs in the till can count as a facility to monitor performance, so the works council must consent in the Netherlands.

assumptions: Boundary: from end of shift to the approved shift totals reaching finance; banking the cash is outside.
Input contract: shift record with till ID, worker, expected and counted totals per tender and note, produced by the till; fallback is the paper slip.
Card terminals are linked to the till or can be.
Shift manager time is outside the counter worker's savings.
Over-and-short views show outlets and tills, not individual scores, unless the works council agrees.

Counting the drawer keeps its full time. s4 keeps 50 because entering each count by denomination is still the worker's own record; only copying the till reading and working out over or short drop. s1 and s3 drop because the till holds the expected totals and takes the terminal totals.
unknowns: Whether the till supports blind shift counts.
Whether finance takes a till export today.
research_questions: What share of overs and shorts are explained by till records?

already_counted.description: Shift manager recounts and approves the shift closing.

incremental.description: Counter worker corrects mistyped counts and uses the paper slip when the till is down.
Finance checks the nightly export and fixes failed days.

approvals.approved_version: The shift balance record for one till and shift, with counted and expected totals per tender and the over or short, exactly as checked and approved by the shift manager in s6c; the nightly job posts it once to the {ERP} sales journal and the {BI} sales view. A recount voids it and needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the terminal cannot be linked, so the card match stays by hand and a printout is still needed for it (21.6); high: the terminal is linked as assumed (39.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check stock of food and supplies, list what is short, receive deliveries and restock the counter.

steps.what: Counter worker checks food and supplies at the counter, fridges and stock room
Counter worker writes shortages and quantities on the order list: on paper today; after the change the worker enters counts on the tablet form and the system proposes quantities
Shift manager checks the list and adjusts the proposed order quantities
Shift manager checks the final order before release: items, quantities, supplier and delivery day
Shift manager places the order in the supplier portal or by phone
Counter worker receives the delivery and carries it in
Counter worker checks the delivery against the delivery note and order
Counter worker restocks counter, fridges and steam table, oldest dates first

tasks.design: A stock count form on a tablet, configured in the {OPS_SYSTEM} or the till's stock module, lists items with par levels; the counter worker enters counts and the system proposes quantities from par minus stock minus open orders. The shift manager adjusts the proposal and checks the final order, an integration sends it to the supplier through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}, and the delivery check ticks off lines on the same tablet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts and orders lived on paper because par levels were in the manager's head and supplier portals took manual entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Stock modules handle par levels and order proposals, and many food suppliers accept orders through portals or files.
tasks.still_hard: Demand swings with weather and events; the manager's judgement on quantities stays, and counting and restocking are physical.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing what is running low during a rush and rotating stock so nothing goes out of date.

ambition.what: Order quantities reviewed against sales every day instead of by eye once or twice a week.

tasks.altitude: The counter worker counts and restocks as before; the manager reviews a proposal instead of building the order.

reach.task: Check stock of prepared ingredients before service
reach.learn: Whether the same par-level form covers prep items.

evidence.claim: Stock modules can compute order proposals from par levels and counts.
A recipe tool costs each recipe from ingredient prices, which gives the ingredient data a usage-based proposal needs.
Food hygiene rules require stock rotation and temperature control; details follow national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the stock check to the counter restocked; supplier invoices and payment are outside.
Input contract: item list with unit, par level and supplier article number, produced by the operations manager; fallback is the paper order list.
Native configuration is tried first: the till or stock system's par-level module before custom code.
Shift manager time is outside the counter worker's savings.
Counting and restocking do not get faster.

Receiving and carrying in (s5) keep their full time. s2 keeps 90 because entering a count for each item is the worker's own record and only working out quantities drops. s6 keeps 80 because only finding the paper order drops; noting each difference is still the worker's own record.
unknowns: Whether suppliers accept orders through a portal or file.
Whether par levels exist anywhere today.
research_questions: How much food is wasted or runs out per week, and does daily ordering change it?

already_counted.description: Shift manager reviews and adjusts the order proposal.

incremental.description: Counter worker fixes count entries and reports items missing from the form.
Operations manager keeps par levels and supplier article numbers current.

approvals.approved_version: The order with items, quantities and delivery day exactly as checked by the shift manager in s3c, sent once by the integration to the named supplier through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: deliveries are still checked on the paper note, so s6 keeps 100 and the upkeep eats the rest (0.1); high: the tablet form is used for count and delivery check (1.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The counter worker keeps serving, counting and restocking; slips, sums and shortage lists drop out.
reach: Shift managers' order approval and cash sign-off
Cooks' work from the kitchen screen
skills_to_grow: Entering counts accurately in the till and stock form
Spotting wrong deal rules or par levels
Explaining an over or short from till records
role.ambitious_version: A counter worker whose counts and orders feed daily stock and cash views the manager trusts, with no paper in between.
